32:3.1.1.text: Walt cooked. Walt always cooked. Nobody else was allowed near the pan. He made us swear off one lake. Said the fishing was lousy. It's a simple stove. You pump it eleven times. Not ten. Eleven.

32:3.2.1.text: I want the mine. I'm not ashamed of it. I want it done by honest men, which is a different thing. The fishing was not lousy. I'm retired. I'm extremely retired.

32:3.4.1.text: Gene took a slide of everything. Forty carousels. I can't throw them out and I can't look at them. Sparky? That was Denny. Flare gun, '86, went off in the canoe. Frank's the electrician, sure. Walt never gave anybody the obvious one.

32:5.1.1.text: Coffee's on. Pie's rhubarb. It's always rhubarb, don't ask.

32:5.1.2.text: That's Walt's pack. He used to drop it right there by the pie case and Gene would trip on it every year. Sit down.

32:5.1.3.text: You're the one who bought the round. Sit. It's on me, which is a first.

32:5.1.4.text: Everybody up here knew him a little. I knew him through Gene. My husband. They went in every August, Gene and the boys and Walt. I fed them when they came out.

32:5.1.5.text: Bob, Frank and Denny. Still go. Eighth of August, in at Sawbill, out the fifteenth, and in here for pie by three. Bob's in Tuesdays and Saturdays. Denny's in every afternoon, he can't help it. Frank's an Ely boy. You'll catch him over at Farm at the crack of dawn, if you're up.

32:5.1.6.text: Gene died in '16. June. His heart. The boys carried him, and Walt. Gene took a slide of everything. Forty carousels. I can't throw them out and I can't look at them.

32:5.1.c4.text: What was Walt like on those trips?

32:5.1.7.text: Loud, if you can believe it. Not loud. Happy. He cooked. Gene said it was the only week a year Walt didn't look over his shoulder. I thought that was a funny thing to say about a man. I think about it now.

32:5.1.8.text: There's something you could do. If you're ever going that way, which nobody is. It's a long way. After the funeral I gave Gene's paddle to Walt. Gene made it with Bob, in the school shop. Walt said he'd take it to Frost and leave it where Gene would want it. Gene loved Frost and could never get the others to go. Walt did it, the next summer. He told me so. I'd like to know it's still there. I'd like to see it. My knees aren't going to Frost.

32:5.1.9.text: Don't make a special trip. Yes, make a special trip. Thank you.

32:5.1.10.text: It is. Gene said that was the point.

32:5.1.11.text: Little Sag, every August, that rock on the point. If you mean his secret places, he didn't tell Gene, and Gene would've told me.

32:5.1.12.text: Go on. Take a bar for the road. Take two, you're thin.

32:5.3.1.text: Look at them. Church men. They look like they're going to a funeral. That's the back of Walt's head, at the pan. That's the only way you ever got him. He took the pictures or he cooked.
32:5.3.1.when: Label (Gene's hand): AUG 85 L. SAG — FIRST

32:5.3.2.text: That black stripe on the thwart. That's the flare. Gene kept that canoe till 2009 for the stripe.

32:5.3.3.text: Frank's girl's wedding. Gene labelled an empty one to make a point. That was Gene.
32:5.3.3.when: Label (Gene's hand): AUG 93 — NO TRIP (empty carousel)

32:5.3.4.text: He wrote that the week they got home. Like he knew. He didn't know. Nobody knows.
32:5.3.4.when: Label (Gene's hand): AUG 11 L. SAG — LAST ONE ALL OF US

32:5.3.5.text: That's the paddle in the canoe. Tied in. You see?

32:5.4.1.text: Walt had a name for every one of them. He never gave anybody the obvious one. Gene was Deacon because he was the only one of those church men who wasn't, really. He came for the walleye. Bob's Teach. You'd think it's the school. It's the stove. He'd explain that stove to a moose. Frank's Whiskey. First morning, first year, Walt poured his bottle into a water jug at the landing. Glass isn't allowed in there. Frank's been carrying good whiskey in plastic for forty years. And Sparky? That was Denny. Flare gun, '86, went off in the canoe. Gene was in the bow. Gene said a word he never said in church. Frank's the electrician, sure. Walt never gave anybody the obvious one.

32:5.5.1.1.text: You're the one with Walt's tent. Carol said. Well. Sit. Mind the oatmeal.

32:5.5.1.2.text: We heard about you! Small town. Not small, it's not a town at all. Small store.

32:5.5.1.3.text: You going to buy the round or just stand there?

32:5.5.1.4.text: Walt's rule. New one buys the first round. Coffee and bars, inside, Carol knows.

32:5.5.1.5.text: Walt's. He made it so he'd never have to buy one. He never bought one.

32:5.5.1.8.text: I'll get it! I'll get it, put it on me.

32:5.5.1.9.text: That's not how the rule goes, Den.

32:5.5.1.10.text: Walt cooked. Walt always cooked. Nobody else was allowed near the pan.

32:5.5.1.11.text: He'd go quiet on the last night. Every trip. Sit on the rock out on the point. We left him be.

32:5.5.1.12.text: He cooked for us twenty-six years and never once let me near the pan. You know? Twenty-six years.

32:5.5.1.13.text: I heard it on the radio. Driving home from Grand Marais, October, and I had to pull over. Where were you that week, Den? Down in Duluth?

32:5.5.1.14.text: Duluth. Tuesday, it was a Tuesday, my sister's thing.

32:5.5.1.16.text: I called him. He didn't say anything for a whole minute. Longest Denny's ever been quiet.

32:5.5.1.18.text: Little Sag. In at Sawbill on the eighth, out on the fifteenth. Same site, the one with the rock. Since 1985, minus one year.

32:5.5.1.20.text: Frank's daughter got married in August. In August.

32:5.5.1.21.text: She's been married thirty-three years. I think it took.

32:5.5.1.c6.text: Did Walt have a favourite spot?

32:5.5.1.23.text: The river. The Isabella. That was Walt's spot. Everybody thought he was a lake man. River man.

32:5.5.1.24.text: He told me the Kek once. He told everybody something.

32:5.5.1.25.text: He didn't tell me anything. I asked once. He said, Teach, you'd draw a diagram.

32:5.5.1.26.text: Retired. Shop teacher. Duluth, then Tofte.

32:5.5.1.27.text: Insurance. Retired. Still can't stop telling people about umbrella policies. Don't get me started.

32:5.5.1.29.text: He kept a notebook? Huh. You'd bring anything like that to us first, right? We're his guys.

32:5.5.1.31.text: I'm only saying. Family, sort of.

32:5.5.1.32.text: Go on, you're losing light. Eighth of August, if you want to see the 473 make old men cry.

32:5.6.1.text: The Isabella. Here, give me your map. That's the site he liked, on the river, below the rapids. And this one. And there's a carry near there, I'll ring that too. And the landing on Isabella Lake. And Bog, ask for the keeper, tell him Denny sent you, he won't know who that is.

32:5.6.2.text: Here. Call me anytime. I mean anytime. I don't sleep. Office number. No office.

32:5.6.3.text: You know what they call me? Go on, Carol's told you. No? Sparky. Eighty-six. I sold safety for a living. You bring a flare. It went off in the bottom of the canoe, Gene in the bow, and the thing skipped across Little Sag like a stone and went out. Gene said a word he never said in church. Burned a stripe on the thwart. Gene's canoe. It's mine now. I kept the stripe. Walt named everybody. Never the obvious one. Frank's the electrician and I'm Sparky. That's Walt.

32:5.6.4.text: I've got the cabin down the Trail all summer. You need a bed between trips, the key's under the minnow bucket. Seriously. It's just me and the radio.

32:5.6.6.text: Was in the neighbourhood! Thought I'd see how you're doing. Did you get to {lake}? Did you find the point? I've got time.

32:5.6.7.text: You want to talk to the mine guys. They knew him longer. They'd know more than us. We just fished.

32:5.6.8.text: Go easy on Carol with the slides. It's hard on her.

32:5.7.3.text: You're up early for a tourist. Huh. That's Walt's.

32:5.7.4.text: Look who's up. You buy coffee here too or just at Sawbill?

32:5.7.5.text: I'm Bob's friend the way a fish is the lake's friend. Forty years. Yeah, I'm Frank.

32:5.7.c3.text: It's got the company's patch on it.

32:5.7.7.text: Lot of shirts in this town have that patch. I'm retired. I'm extremely retired.

32:5.7.8.text: I want the mine. I'm not ashamed of it. I want it done by honest men, which is a different thing. My daughter's boy drives truck in the Bakken. Comes home at Christmas smelling like diesel. You tell him about wilderness.

32:5.7.c5.text: Did Walt ever tell you where he was going?

32:5.7.9.text: The Kek. Summer of '19, July, he calls me up out of nowhere and says he's going to the Kek in August, don't tell anybody. The Kek. At his age. Like it was a secret. The Kek's not a secret, there's a trail of Cities people from here to there. I didn't tell anybody. Who would I tell. Nobody asked me.

32:5.7.10.text: Walt thought everybody was watching him. Walt thought the Forest Service was watching him. Half the time he was right.

32:5.7.11.text: I'm going to bed. Some of us work n— Some of us are tired.

32:5.8.1.text: Tuesday. Board's got new walleye money on it. Deb's paying better than Bev.

32:5.8.2.text: You've been talking to Carol. It's a simple stove. You pump it eleven times. Not ten. Eleven. I said it once, in 1986, and that was that.

32:5.8.3.text: Matt. Leukaemia, when he was eleven. Beat it. Then it came back in '17. He was thirty, between jobs, no insurance. Rochester. Two years of it. Got paid for somehow, thank God. Denny didn't say much and we never asked. A policy, he said. He'd know, it was his line. Matt's fine. Two girls. Coaches. You'd never know.

32:5.8.c3.text: Did Walt ever say he was worried?

32:5.8.4.text: Well. August of '19. He met us at the landing like he always did. Thermos, bars. Shook every hand. Then at the cars he takes me by the elbow, like this, and he says, Bob, one of us talks to the wrong people. Don't ask me which. So I didn't.

32:5.8.5.text: I'm seventy-four. I've known those men forty years. I made myself not do the arithmetic. You can do that, if you practise.

32:5.8.6.text: No. No. You don't get that from me.

32:5.8.7.text: Frank guards their parking lot nights. Has since '19. He thinks we don't know. Denny's the one who found out, actually. Frank would die before he'd talk. He'd die of being Frank first.

32:5.9.1.1.text: You're on ours. Nine to a permit and we're three. I already called the ranger station. Don't look at me like that, Bob, somebody had to.

32:5.9.1.2.text: Nobody was looking at you, Den.

32:5.9.1.3.text: Bob does the permit. Bob's done the permit since 1988. I did one thing.

32:5.9.2.2.text: You found us. Of course you did. Sit.

32:5.9.2.5.text: Oh, I'm not supposed to. Give me two.

32:5.9.3.1.text: Every year it was free. Three years it wasn't, and we sat across the bay and glared at whoever had it.

32:5.9.3.2.text: One year it was a youth group. Twelve kids. We glared at children.

32:5.9.3.4.text: I sold safety for a living! You bring a flare!

32:5.9.3.7.text: Swamped, no paddle. Walt? Walt didn't lose paddles. He lost sunglasses. Not paddles.

32:5.9.3.10.text: He'd hate this. Us sitting around talking about him like he's a story.

32:5.9.3.11.text: Ballgame. They're losing. They've been losing since 1991. I listen anyway. Somebody has to.

32:5.9.3.12.text: Walt used to say Sparky kept us up with the radio.

32:5.9.3.14.text: Walt threw the radio in the lake in 2004.

32:5.9.3.15.text: And then he went in and got it. That's love.

32:5.9.4.1.text: Walt's. We bring it. Nobody's cooked in it since 2011. Somebody has to.

32:5.9.4.4.text: That's not how he did it. That's not bad.

32:5.9.4.6.text: Keep it in the pack till the fifteenth. Then give it back. Then we'll see about next year.

32:5.9.5.1.text: Laker bet. Walt's spoons. One each. Deep hole off the island, out past the point. Biggest fish buys the round on the fifteenth. Walt's other rule. He said a man that lucky can afford it.

32:5.9.5.2.text: I'm not trolling. I've got the ballgame. I'll judge.

32:5.9.5.3.text: Denny judges every year. Denny has never once judged correctly.

32:5.9.6.1.text: You know he took us somewhere else once. One time. September.

32:5.9.6.3.text: I'm not saying where. I swore on the coffee. I'm saying it happened.

32:5.9.6.4.text: Ninety-eight. September. Walt, Gene, me and Frank. In at Little Gabbro. Across Bald Eagle, which is a big grey lake that wants you dead in the afternoon. Then a lake we don't name.
32:5.9.6.4.if: after a while, to the line in the water

32:5.9.6.6.text: He said it had lousy fishing. He made us swear off it. On the coffee.

32:5.9.6.7.text: The fishing was not lousy. We had walleye coming out of our ears. Gene's got a picture.

32:5.9.6.8.text: Second day he goes off on his own. Says he's going to look at a beaver dam in the east bay. Gone half the day. Comes back wet to the knees. No fish. Laughing.

32:5.9.6.9.text: Creek comes in there under the dam. There's a notch in the ridge behind it, like somebody took a bite out. I remember the notch. I don't remember my own kids' birthdays but I remember the notch.

32:5.9.6.10.text: Thirteen years of Little Sag and then one September he takes us there, and never again, and we're not to say. I thought it was a joke for a long time. I don't know what I think now.

32:5.9.6.11.text: Denny missed that one. Kid was sick. Matt. Leukaemia, eleven years old. Walt drove down to Duluth to see him after. Sat with him a whole afternoon. Didn't tell any of us; Denny told us.

32:5.9.6.12.text: We don't tell it in camp. Den gets — he missed it. It's a sore spot.

32:5.9.6.13.text: So we don't tell it in camp.

32:5.9.6.15.text: On the coffee. Sorry. Past Bald Eagle. That's all you get out of two old men in a boat.

32:5.9.6.16.text: Put it on me, Carol. Put it all on me.

32:5.9.8.2.text: He'd say it's a waste of good whiskey.

32:5.9.8.4.text: Nobody sits there the last night.

32:5.10.c3.text: A sapling, cut and lashed up

32:5.11.1.text: Oh, {lake}! Good one. Here — — and the site on the point, and there's a walleye hole, I'll ring that. Call me when you're back. I mean it.

32:5.11.2.text: {lake}? In this wind? Suit yourself. Good walleye. Don't tell anybody I said.

32:5.11.3.text: {lake}. Take the long way. Take a picture of the cliffs for me.

32:5.12.c1.text: When did you last talk to Walt?

32:5.13.1.text: Frank guards their lot nights. He'd die before he'd talk.

32:5.13.c1.text: You work nights for the company. Bob knows.

32:5.13.2.text: Course Bob knows. Bob knows everything, he just doesn't say it, it's very irritating. Since '19. Part-time. Nights. I walk around a parking lot with a flashlight and I check the doors. The pension's fine. I just — I'm seventy-two, I don't like sitting in a house. I didn't want them to think — with Walt. You know. One of us working for the outfit he hated.

32:5.13.3.text: Once. Summer of '19. There's a security office. Door's supposed to be locked. It wasn't. Folder on the desk. *Haapala, W.* That's all I read, the front. I put it back where it was and locked the door from the inside and I told nobody. For the job. I've thought about that every day since October. It's still there. Bottom drawer. *Closed.* They don't throw anything out. They're a mining company.

32:5.13.4.text: Could I. I'm on Thursday. Come back Friday.

32:5.13.c5.text: I saw you in the lot one night. With a man in a clean coat.

32:5.13.6.text: You and everybody on the highway. That's their security fella. Comes by once a month to tell me how to hold a flashlight. That night he wanted to know was I leaving the office door unlocked. I said no. Which was a lie, once. Summer of '19.

32:5.14.c2.text: You work for them and you lied about it.

32:5.15.c1.text: You called the bunkhouse that night. Your number's on Marlys's pad.

32:5.15.1.text: I called him lots. Sundays. I told you, we talked Sundays.

32:5.15.2.text: There's programs. For — there's assistance. There was a policy.

32:5.15.c3.text: I told you {lake}. Two days later they were on {lake}.

32:5.15.3.text: I tell everybody everything. I talk at the gas station. Ask anybody.

32:5.15.c4.text: Walt told you the river. They went to the river.
32:5.15.c4.if: nicknames + N34–35 (+ Isabella camp, if found)

32:5.15.4.text: The river was his spot. Everybody knew the river was his spot.

32:5.15.c5.text: How do you know he said he was in all week?

32:5.15.5.text: Somebody said. Marlys. Somebody at the funeral.

32:5.15.c6.text: Your sister's thing was a Tuesday. The seventeenth was a Thursday.

32:5.15.6.text: Tuesday, Thursday. It's seven years. Who remembers a day.

32:5.15.7.text: It is. It is a nice night.

32:5.15.c11.text: He told only you the river.

32:5.15.c13.text: You know every number to the dollar, Den. You don't know a Thursday?

32:5.15.c15.text: When they ask, you tell them what I tell you.

32:5.15.c16.text: Bob and Frank are going to know.

32:5.15.c17.text: I'm not going to say anything.

32:5.16.1.c1.text: The river. Tell them I talk about the river.

32:5.16.1.2.text: The river. That's what he told me. He told me the river. He knew, didn't he. That summer. He knew it was me.

32:5.16.1.3.text: And he still picked up the phone. He said *in all week* and he was gone by midnight. He lied to me. Good. Good for him.

32:5.16.1.4.text: He knew. Walt knew everything. He knew where the fish were in a lake he'd never seen.

32:5.16.1.c4.text: Tell them I've gone home for the season.

32:5.16.1.7.text: You don't know him. Okay. Okay. I owe Walt a lie. I can do one lie.

32:5.16.1.8.text: He asked did you ever say *far end*. I said you say *walleye* a lot.

32:5.16.1.9.text: They've got a man sitting at the Pietro end now. He told me like I'd care.

32:5.16.1.10.text: He asked me were you scared. I said you seemed like a fella who wasn't scared enough.

32:5.16.2.1.text: Now? Let me tell them. Can I tell them? I should be the one.

32:5.16.2.2.text: Bob. Frank. I have to say a thing. I called the bunkhouse that night.

32:5.16.2.3.text: I've been walking their parking lot two years thinking if anybody finds out where I work, they'll think it's me. It was you.

32:5.16.2.4.text: Well. I made myself not do the arithmetic, Den. Seven years. I practised.

32:5.16.2.6.text: I know about Matt. I drove you to Rochester twice. We paddle out together tomorrow. All three. Nobody's on the water alone. That's the rule now. After that I don't know, Den. I don't know.

32:5.16.2.7.text: You should go to your own site.

32:5.16.3.1.text: That's worse. You know that's worse? Thank you. I'll stop. Telling him. Whatever you say I'll forget. I'll tell him I lost track of you. I'm an old man, I lose track.

32:6.c1.text: Somebody told them where Walt was.

32:6.1.text: Sparky is Denny. Whiskey is Frank. Walt never gave anybody the obvious one.

32:6.2.text: Walt told Whiskey the Kek and Sparky the river. The green Kevlar went to the river. Nobody came to the Kek.

32:6.3.text: Denny said it was a Tuesday. The 17th was a Thursday.

32:6.4.text: Denny knows Walt said he was in all week. That's on the last page. Who else would know?

32:6.5.text: Denny brought it up himself: *Somebody talked.*

32:6.6.text: Denny sent me to Walt's spot on the river. Somebody had camped there in August 2019 with a radio.

32:6.8.text: The number on Marlys's pad is the number on Denny's card.

32:6.9.text: Matt Rask was sick again from 2017, uninsured. Two years in Rochester. It got paid for somehow.

32:6.10.text: Walt to Bob, August 2019: *One of us talks to the wrong people.*

32:6.11.text: Someone, *src*, told them where he was going. Paid every month.

32:6.12.text: Frank wears the company's patch. He says he's retired.

32:6.13.text: Frank, at night, in the company's lot, talking with a man in a clean coat.

32:10.1.text: Eighth of August. Sawbill. You're buying. Keep it. It's not a loan anymore.

32:10.2.text: I wanted the mine. I still want the mine. Now it's a fair fight. They let the security outfit go. New outfit, same lot. Better coffee.

32:10.3.text: Denny sent a card at Christmas. We sent one back. That's where it is.

32:10.4.text: Maybe next year. Maybe. Don't push.

32:10.6.text: I wanted the mine. Not like this. They're building it on a lie, and they paid you for the lie.
